evidence.quote:
/// OrderBy + filter coverage for all remaining uncovered ColumnOrderings and

findings.why: Every one of these 474 tests inserts exactly one row in setUp, then calls orderBy/filter/computedField/withFields and asserts only `hasLength(1)`/`isNotEmpty`/`isA<List<...>>`. Confirmed by exhaustive grep: zero occurrences anywhere in the 2435-line orderby file of `hasLength(0)`, `hasLength(2)`, or `equals([...])` — no test ever inserts a second, differently-ordered or non-matching row, so a broken `.asc()`/`.desc()` (or a filter predicate that matches everything, or one that silently no-ops) still returns the single seeded row and the test stays green. Ran both the smallest (crossref_filter_test.dart) and largest (orderby_test.dart) files in this session: 26/26 and 283/283 pass today, so this is 474 currently-green CI checkmarks that give zero regression protection for the very ordering/filtering behavior their names promise. Compounding it: `grep -rl '\.managers\.' lib/` returns 0 files — the Drift-generated Manager API under test (`db.managers.*`) has no caller anywhere in production code; the app queries through hand-written DAOs instead. This is ~5900 lines of test code (this batch alone) written to drive `flutter test --coverage` numbers up against a generated-code surface the app never exercises, at real cost: CI/build time on every run, and reviewer/agent attention budget on every future change to user_database.dart (per AG-3's own rationale about per-file read budgets).
findings.recommendation: Delete this suite — `db.managers.*` has no production caller, so there is no behavior left to protect. If the underlying goal was raising `user_database.g.dart` line-coverage numbers, exclude generated files from the coverage gate instead (e.g. `lcov --remove coverage/lcov.info '*.g.dart' '*.freezed.dart'` in the coverage make target) rather than writing assertion-free tests. If any ordering/filtering behavior here genuinely needs protecting because a DAO wraps it, move that coverage to the DAO's own test file with real assertions: insert ≥2 rows with distinct sort keys and assert exact order via `equals([...])`, and insert ≥1 matching + ≥1 non-matching row per filter test and assert the non-matching row is excluded.

Coverage tooling (`make test` / CI) excludes `*.g.dart` and `*.freezed.dart` from the coverage report, removing the incentive that produced this suite.

findings.why: 41 of the file's 42 tests (every test except 'filter by displayName' at line 175-183) assert only isNotNull on a getter whose return type is non-nullable ($$XTableProcessedTableManager, confirmed by grepping user_database.g.dart — never `?`), or isNotEmpty on rows that come from the base table regardless of the specific ref/prefetch-flag/computedField under test. Verified line 23 (`import 'package:drift/drift.dart' hide isNotNull, isNull;`) confirms these are flutter_test's boolean matchers, not SQL builders. Concretely: deleting `curriculumScopesRefs: true` from the prefetch call at line 374, or breaking the FK the getter filters on in user_database.dart, would not fail any of these tests — the isNotNull can only fail via an exception (impossible given the type), and isNotEmpty is satisfied by the parent row alone. The file's own header claims this suite 'covers' the References/prefetch classes; it cannot detect a broken relationship or prefetch join.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite assertions to depend on the specific thing under test: e.g. call `.get()` on the returned manager and assert the rows' FK column equals the parent id used in setUp, or assert a real row count/field value through the prefetched cache, or compare a flag-on vs flag-off query to show the flag changed behavior.

findings.title: Guard FirebaseAuthGatewayImpl link/reauth methods against silent no-op on null currentUser
findings.why: If currentUser is null when these fire (expired/revoked anonymous session, or a UI race), the `?.` swallows the call and the method returns a normally-completed Future<void> — no exception, no signal that nothing happened. The one real caller (features/account/data/repositories/auth_repository_impl.dart:129-140 `linkGoogleProvider`/`linkEmailProvider`/`reauthenticateWithGoogle`) just awaits and reports success with nothing to double-check. That directly undercuts AU-1: linking must actually run against the anonymous uid so its offline data carries over; a silent no-op leaves the account anonymous while the user believes it's now permanent, and Identity Platform auto-deletes unlinked anonymous accounts after 30 days (AU-3's rationale), which can permanently orphan the child's offline learning history. Every sibling precondition check in this same file (deleteCurrentUser:172-176, updatePassword:181-186, reauthenticateWithEmail:192-199, sendEmailVerification:100-104) throws `StateError` instead of silently no-op'ing; the one genuinely-intentional no-op in the file (`updateDisplayName`) is declared as such by an explicit 'is a no-op when no user is signed in' test — these three methods have neither the guard nor a test declaring the no-op intentional, which is the tell that it's an oversight, not a design choice.
findings.recommendation: Add the same `if (user == null) throw ...` guard used elsewhere in this file before calling linkWithCredential/reauthenticateWithCredential in all three methods (ideally throwing the typed exception recommended in the companion EH-5 finding rather than another StateError). Add regression tests mirroring the existing 'throws when no user is signed in' pattern for linkWithGoogleIdToken, linkWithEmailAndPassword, and reauthenticateWithGoogleIdToken.

findings.recommendation: Mirror the null-check-and-throw pattern used elsewhere in the file (or the typed exception recommended in the EH-5 finding) instead of force-unwrapping credential.user.

findings.title: Wrap TrackLearningOrderDao.upsertOrder's per-row insert loop and its repository call sites in one transaction/batch

evidence.quote:
Future<void> upsertOrder(int trackId, List<String> refs) async {
    for (var i = 0; i < refs.length; i++) {

findings.why: upsertOrder writes N rows via an awaited for-loop with no db.transaction()/db.batch() wrapper, and its only callers (saveSedarimOrder/saveMasechtosOrder/resetToDefault) then make a second, entirely separate write (stampReorderAt) with no shared transaction either. A user reordering a full masechta/seder (which can be dozens to hundreds of refs) who has the app killed mid-reorder (OS memory pressure, backgrounding kill — routine on mobile) is left with a partially-old/partially-new sortOrder sequence and no error anywhere. getByTrack() then feeds that corrupted order straight into the daily learning projection, producing skipped or repeated study segments with zero user-visible signal that anything went wrong. Even when upsertOrder itself completes, dying before the separate stampReorderAt call leaves a stale lastReorderAt, breaking the reorder-amnesty logic documented at architecture §10.1. This is discovered via track_learning_order_dao_test.dart (in this batch), which covers the happy path only and has no test for interrupted/partial writes.
findings.recommendation: Replace the for-loop in upsertOrder with a single db.batch((b) { for (...) b.insert(trackLearningOrder, ..., onConflict: ...); }) — Drift batches are atomic, satisfying DB-2 and DB-3 in one change. In the repository, wrap the order-write + stampReorderAt call of saveSedarimOrder/saveMasechtosOrder/resetToDefault in one _database.transaction(...) so the pair commits or rolls back together.
acceptance_criteria: TrackLearningOrderDao.upsertOrder issues one db.batch() instead of an awaited per-row loop.
saveSedarimOrder, saveMasechtosOrder, and resetToDefault each wrap their order-write + stampReorderAt call in a single db.transaction().
New regression test asserts the reorder write is all-or-nothing (e.g. inject a failure partway through a multi-ref batch and assert zero rows changed / the pre-reorder order is intact).

No Rule-0 checker exists yet for this class of bug (DB-2/DB-3 are [P]ending) — note the gap; a grep for `for (` followed within a few lines by `await into(` or `await (db.update`/`await (db.delete` inside lib/core/database/daos/**/*.dart would catch this pattern cheaply.

findings.title: Deduplicate 5 shadowed top-level keys in app_he.arb/app_en.arb — one silently kills a zero-task notification branch
findings.rule: Rule 0 gap (no duplicate-key checker for ARB files)
findings.why: JSON's last-key-wins behavior is confirmed against the generated Dart output: lib/l10n/app_localizations_he.dart's todaysLearning(count), errorLoadingTasks(error) and notificationReminderBody(taskCount, curriculumCount) all match the SECOND (later) ARB definition, not the first. No checker anywhere (make audit, arb-parity, flutter analyze) catches a duplicate top-level key within a single ARB file, so 3 of the 5 duplicate pairs carry genuinely different text: an editor who fixes the first (now-dead) copy of todaysLearning or errorLoadingTasks has the fix silently discarded. Worse, notificationReminderBody's line-1765 definition had a deliberately-written zero-task branch (he: 'אין משימות להיום — שמרו על הרצף!' / en: 'No tasks today — stay on track!'); a later duplicate insertion at line 2636/2834 (identical pattern in app_en.arb) replaced it with a two-way plural that has no zero case at all. It is not live-broken today only because the sole caller, lib/features/notifications/presentation/providers/notification_providers.dart:517, has an unrelated 'D2 fix' guard (`if (taskCount == 0) { cancel; return; }`) that happens to prevent taskCount=0 from ever reaching the l10n call — if that guard is ever removed or a second caller is added, Intl.pluralLogic falls to `other` and produces 'You have 0 tasks…' instead of the friendly copy that still sits, unused, in the file. The identical 5-key duplicate set exists in app_en.arb too, confirming this is a systemic missing-checker gap, not a one-off typo.
findings.recommendation: Add a Rule-0 checker (tool/ script or a test/l10n/ test) that fails when any top-level key string appears more than once in app_en.arb or app_he.arb, wired into make audit/ci. Then resolve the 5 duplicates: keep todaysLearning's parameterized form (matches its @todaysLearning metadata), keep errorLoadingTasks's live copy or fix the grammar deliberately, and decide whether notificationReminderBody's zero-task branch should be restored (and its caller's guard removed) or the dead ARB text deleted — don't leave orphaned content either way.
acceptance_criteria: A new checker/test fails when a top-level ARB key is duplicated, and is part of make audit or make ci.
app_en.arb and app_he.arb each contain todaysLearning, errorLoadingTasks, today, notificationReminderTitle, and notificationReminderBody exactly once.
notificationReminderBody's zero-task branch is either wired to a real caller or its vestigial ARB text is removed — no orphaned/unused ICU branch remains.

findings.why: Both files were written to pin fixes for shipped, user-visible bugs (AN-6: DASHBOARD nav label truncates at font_scale 1.3; AN-8: a signed-in account chip overlays the sign-in screen), but neither imports the file it claims to guard. app_shell_an6_test.dart's only imports are flutter/material.dart and flutter_test.dart — it defines and tests _ShellNavItemReplica, a hand-copied literal duplicate of the real (private) _ShellNavItem in lib/app/router/app_shell.dart:341-365; today the two happen to share the same padding/margin values, but nothing keeps them in sync. persistent_switcher_scaffold_an8_test.dart's only import is flutter_test.dart — its _authRouteNames set duplicates the literal set inside the real _isAuthSurface() at lib/app/router/persistent_switcher_scaffold.dart:92-98, and every assertion (e.g. expect(_authRouteNames.contains('SignInRoute'), isTrue)) is tautologically true by construction, since the test built the set itself. findings.title: Stop using app_localizations_coverage_test.dart's 1482 zero-assertion lines to pad the CI coverage floor over generated l10n code
findings.rule: TQ-8 / Rule 0 (coverage floor's stated generated-file exclusion is unenforced)

findings.title: Constrain AnalyticsService.logEvent to the AnalyticsEvent catalog — LogEvents-sourced calls leak profile_id and content identifiers to Firebase Analytics

evidence.quote: // Typed string constants for structured log event names.

findings.why: AnalyticsService.logEvent(String name, ...) accepts any bare string, so nothing stops a caller from importing LogEvents — documented in its own header as 'structured log event names' for AppLogger, not an analytics catalog — and piping it straight into real Firebase Analytics. Grepping every `.logEvent(` call site in lib/ shows ~15 places do exactly this, bypassing the audited 12-event AnalyticsEvent catalog and its PV-1 review entirely. At least 7 of those sites attach identifying data: outbox_processor.dart fires sync_outbox_dead_lettered with entity_key = '${profileId}:${sefariaRef}:${stageId}:${trackType}:${curriculumId}' (confirmed composition in completion_writer.dart:747) for every dead-lettered completion row — combining the per-child profile id with the exact Torah/Mishnah reference the child was studying in one string; pull_pipeline.dart fires sync_merge_router_halt with a bare profile_id; tutor_pin_service.dart fires tutor_pin_set with a bare profile_id; tutor_audit_log_writer.dart fires tutor_action_recorded with a 'target' field whose own documented shape is a resource path like 'profile/42.displayName' (line 130) — i.e. the profile id again, now attached to a description of what was changed; sync_orchestrator.dart fires sync_pull_failed and sync_listener_error with the raw exception's `.toString()`, which for Firestore permission/not-found errors routinely embeds the full document resource path (profiles/{id}/completions/{ref}). In release/profile builds analyticsServiceProvider resolves to the real FirebaseAnalyticsService (analytics_provider.dart), whose logEvent forwards `parameters` verbatim with zero redaction (firebase_analytics_service.dart:29-32) — so every one of these fires a real event to Google's servers. This is materially worse than the two baselined single-field leaks (bare sefaria_ref, bare profile_id in analytics_service.dart) because several of these sites combine per-child identity with content/action detail in one uncatalogued, unreviewed string, and remains a live COPPA/GDPR-K risk independent of the separately-baselined PV-3 consent-gating gap (fixing consent gating controls whether these fire at all, not what's inside them once a user has consented).
findings.recommendation: Change AnalyticsService.logEvent's name parameter from bare String to a closed type sourced only from AnalyticsEvent (e.g. an extension type/sealed wrapper), add a Rule-0 grep/lint that fails CI on any `.logEvent(` call whose first argument isn't `AnalyticsEvent.<x>`, and triage the 7 cited sites: either drop the identifying parameter and keep these as AppLogger-only structured logs (most already have a parallel LogEvents-based AppLogger call right next to the analytics one), or promote them into AnalyticsEvent with PV-1-safe parameters (counts/enums/booleans only) and route error detail through a stable EH-5 error-code enum instead of `.toString()`.
acceptance_criteria: A checker (grep in make audit, or a working custom_lint rule) fails with file:line on any AnalyticsService.logEvent(...)/.logEvent( call whose event-name argument is not an AnalyticsEvent member
entity_key/profile_id/target/error-text parameters are removed, hashed, or replaced with a coarse enum at all 7 cited call sites

A regression test asserts FakeAnalyticsService-captured params for outbox_dead_lettered, merge_router_halt, pull_failed, listener_error, tutor_pin_set, and tutor_action_recorded never contain a raw profileId, sefariaRef, or exception string

findings.title: Type streak_milestone_analytics_observer.dart's two catch blocks to Exception — bare Object catches swallow Error subtypes as warnings
findings.why: Neither catch has an `on X` clause, so both also catch Dart Error subtypes (NoSuchMethodError, TypeError, RangeError, StateError) that signal genuine programming bugs, not recoverable runtime conditions — exactly what EH-4 says never to catch. A bug in StreakStateProvider or an unexpected state shape gets downgraded to a single logger.warning(...) call (not even error/critical) and the loop or stream quietly continues or ends — no crash, no Crashlytics report, nothing but a line in a 2000-entry ring buffer nobody reviews outside 'Send Diagnostic Logs'. This provider runs unconditionally in the app shell every session (per its own doc comment), so a regression here has zero blast-radius signal to catch it.
findings.recommendation: Narrow both catches to `on Exception catch (e, st)` (or the specific exception types StreakStateProvider/AnalyticsService can throw) and let Error subtypes propagate to the zone's onError handler like the rest of the app.
acceptance_criteria: Both catch clauses in streak_milestone_analytics_observer.dart use `on Exception catch` (or a named typed exception), not bare `catch (e, st)`
streak_milestone_analytics_observer_test.dart's existing R6-3 tests still pass unchanged (they throw plain Exception, not Error)

findings.title: Guard CrashlyticsService's unawaited analytics calls with catchError — unguarded rejection can re-enter the runZonedGuarded fatal-error handler
findings.why: main.dart wraps the whole app in runZonedGuarded whose error callback (lines 26-31) calls _crashlytics.recordError(...) — which is FirebaseCrashlyticsService.recordError, firing `unawaited(_analytics.logCrashReported(...))` with no .catchError attached at either of the two sites cited. If the Firebase Analytics plugin call itself rejects (platform-channel failure, SDK not yet initialized, offline queue full), that unhandled Future error is delivered back into the very same Zone installed by runZonedGuarded, invoking the identical error callback again, which calls recordError again, firing another unawaited call — a self-feeding loop precisely at the moment (an active fatal-crash report) when the app's error-handling path most needs to be inert. Contrast with streak_milestone_analytics_observer.dart in the same directory tree, which does guard its own fire-and-forget analytics call with `.catchError(...)` (line 63-70) — the inconsistency shows this omission wasn't a deliberate choice. Needs runtime confirmation: inject an AnalyticsService whose logCrashReported always rejects inside a runZonedGuarded harness and observe whether recordError re-enters.
findings.recommendation: Add `.catchError((_, __) {})` (or route failures through AppLogger only) to both unawaited(_analytics.logCrashReported(...)) calls in crashlytics_service.dart, matching the guard pattern already used in streak_milestone_analytics_observer.dart.
acceptance_criteria: Both fire-and-forget analytics calls in crashlytics_service.dart have an attached .catchError/try-catch so a rejected Future never re-enters the zone's onError
A regression test injects an AnalyticsService whose logCrashReported always throws, calls recordError once, and asserts it is not invoked a second time

findings.title: Inject an overridable clock into streakMilestoneAnalyticsObserverProvider instead of hardcoding SystemLocalDayClock
findings.why: The observer instantiates `const SystemLocalDayClock()` directly rather than watching an injectable clock — the codebase already has this seam elsewhere (e.g. outbox_providers.dart reads `ref.watch(localDayClockProvider)`). Because the observer can't be handed a fixed clock in tests, the happy-path test has to anchor seeded data to real `DateTime.now()` and then poll every 20ms for up to 5 real seconds waiting for the milestone to fire, instead of asserting deterministically against a fixed instant. The test's own comment documents this was already a source of past flakiness ('silently breaks the moment the calendar advances', 'failed in isolation') — the current polling approach is less likely to fail, not deterministic, and burns up to 5 real seconds per run.
findings.recommendation: Thread a LocalDayClock through the provider (watch a clock provider, mirroring outbox_providers.dart) so tests can override with a fixed clock and assert the milestone fires on an exact expected tick without polling.
acceptance_criteria: streak_milestone_analytics_observer_test.dart's happy-path test uses a fixed/injected clock instead of DateTime.now(), with no wall-clock polling loop

findings.title: Fix ScheduleSpec.weekly/.rolling to throw ArgumentError instead of assert() (silently unenforced in release builds)

evidence.quote: Throws [ArgumentError] when [daysOfWeek] is empty or contains values

findings.why: WeeklySchedule and RollingSchedule enforce their invariants with Dart `assert()`, which the compiler strips out of release builds entirely (only active in debug/profile). Both factory doc comments explicitly promise 'Throws ArgumentError' — that promise is false in the exact build users run. `fromParts` (same file, line 63) feeds `daysOfWeek ?? const []` directly into `WeeklySchedule(...)` whenever the DB/JSON column is null, and the independent JSON codec path in stage_definition_repository_impl.dart:346-349 does the same for a missing `days_of_week`/`days` key, wrapped in a try/catch that only rescues the debug-mode AssertionError — in release it silently produces a `WeeklySchedule([])`. A stage with an empty day-list never matches any weekday, so its chazara review permanently stops being scheduled with no error, no log, and no user-facing signal.
findings.recommendation: Replace both asserts with explicit `if (...) throw ArgumentError(...)` (matching the pattern already used correctly by ScopeLevel/StageOrder/Pin/DayKind/CalendarSystem in the same directory) so the invariant holds in release builds too.

findings.title: Make ScheduleSpec's delayDays/daysOfWeek/rollingWindowSize getters exhaustive instead of using a `_` catch-all
findings.why: EH-6 requires sealed-type switches to be exhaustive with no `default:`/`_` arm, precisely so the compiler forces every call site to be revisited when a new subtype is added. All three convenience getters on the sealed ScheduleSpec base class use `_ =>` to cover 'the other two variants' instead of naming them. The file's own docstring says a W3.27 migration to a single JSON `schedule` column is coming and will touch this exact codec — when that (or any future) change adds a 4th ScheduleSpec variant, these three getters will compile cleanly and silently return 0/null/null for it instead of forcing a compile error, which is exactly the failure mode sealed classes exist to prevent.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite each getter with an explicit arm per subtype (e.g. `WeeklySchedule() => 0, RollingSchedule() => 0` instead of `_ => 0`) so adding a new variant breaks the build until these getters are updated.
acceptance_criteria: delayDays/daysOfWeek/rollingWindowSize each list DelaySchedule/WeeklySchedule/RollingSchedule explicitly with no `_`/`default` arm.

findings.title: Fix SefariaRef.titlePart/addressPart to match the documented chapter:verse split (or fix the docs)
findings.rule: Evans (ubiquitous-language contract) / TQ-7-TQ-8 spirit (test encodes the bug instead of catching it)
findings.why: The class docstring's own worked example says titlePart of "Mishnah Berakhot 1:1" is "Mishnah Berakhot" (address "1:1"). The `_splitTail` regex only strips a single trailing digit run (optionally +1 letter), so it can never cross the ':' in a chapter:verse address — for that exact documented example it actually produces titlePart == "Mishnah Berakhot 1:" and addressPart == "1". The test file's own inline comment ('let's assert what we actually produce... The SefariaRef titlePart splits on the LAST pure-numeric token') shows the author noticed the mismatch and wrote the test to lock in the wrong output rather than fix the regex or the docs. Mishnah/Tanach chapter:verse is the single most common ref shape in this Torah-study app, so any future caller of titlePart/addressPart (currently unused in production) inherits silently wrong output for the primary case, with a green regression test giving false confidence.
findings.recommendation: Either extend `_splitTail` to also recognize a `\d+:\d+` chapter:verse tail as one address token, or correct the docstring to describe the actual single-digit-run behavior — then update the test to assert the corrected contract, not the current output.
acceptance_criteria: SefariaRef.parse('Mishnah Berakhot 1:1').titlePart equals whatever the corrected docstring promises (either 'Mishnah Berakhot' with the regex fixed, or the docstring rewritten to match current behavior).

findings.title: Migrate core/domain/value_objects/ hand-written ==/hashCode/toString classes to @freezed
findings.rule: Naming/placement — "Domain/state models are immutable @freezed classes; never hand-write ==/hashCode for data classes"
findings.why: Every non-enum class in this batch (Pin; ProgramStartingPosition; DelaySchedule/WeeklySchedule/RollingSchedule; ScopeLevel/ScopeValue/CurriculumScope; SefariaRef; StageOrder; StudyDayPattern — 10 classes across 7 files) hand-writes operator==/hashCode/toString rather than using @freezed, contrary to the stated codebase convention. All the ones I traced are currently correct, so this is not a live bug, but it is the exact pattern the standard calls out as risky: every future field addition to any of these classes requires manually keeping three methods in sync by hand with no compiler help, whereas @freezed generates all three from the field list and can't drift.
findings.recommendation: Migrate these VOs to @freezed where the validating-factory pattern (private const constructor + public validating factory) fits, which all of these already structurally resemble; note any VO where freezed genuinely doesn't fit as a documented exception in coding-standards.md rather than leaving it a silent inconsistency.
acceptance_criteria: New or materially-changed value objects in core/domain/value_objects/ use @freezed, or coding-standards.md documents an explicit lightweight-VO exception.
No behavior change: existing equality/hashCode/toString tests for these 7 files continue passing unmodified after any migration.

findings.title: Scope DAO id-based get/update/delete methods to profileId — goal_dao, bookmark_dao, learning_order_dao, stage_dao, and BaseDao.getById all mutate by bare row id

evidence.quote:
Future<Row?> getById(int id) {
    final query = select(table)..where((t) => idColumn(t).equals(id))
**Enforcement:** `make audit` flags any user-DB table without a `profileId` column.

findings.why: Every table these DAOs sit on (curriculum_tracks, bookmarks, goals, learning_order, stage_definitions, …) declares profileId only in a secondary `uniqueKeys`/`@TableIndex`, not in Drift's actual `primaryKey` — the real PK is a bare autoincrement `id` (verified directly in lib/core/database/tables/*.dart). docs/coding-standards.md:663-665 names this an explicit invariant ("No user-facing Drift table may use a single-column autoincrement primary key without also specifying profileId as part of a composite key override") and claims it is enforced by `make audit`; the learning_tracker/Makefile audit target (22 numbered greps, lines 277-505) has no such check — the claim is false. Because the PK is bare id, `getById`/`update…().replace()`/`delete…(id)` never filter by profileId, so any caller that obtains a foreign profile's numeric id (stale provider state after a profile switch, a sync-merge bug, a crafted id) can read/overwrite/delete another profile's row. This is not theoretical: lib/features/scheduler/data/repositories/goal_repository_impl.dart's updateGoal/deleteGoal fetch `goalDao.getGoalById(goalId)` and then unconditionally mutate/delete without ever comparing `existing.profileId` to the repository's own bound profile — the DAO provides zero defense-in-depth and this caller adds none either. (Contrast: bookmark_repository_impl.setBookmark re-derives the id via a profileId-checked lookup first, so it's safe — the inconsistency across callers is exactly what a shared, enforced invariant is supposed to prevent.)
findings.recommendation: Add profileId as an explicit parameter to every id-based get/update/delete DAO method in this batch (or drop BaseDao.getById/replace-by-id entirely in favor of profileId-qualified variants) and filter the WHERE/replace target on it. Fix or remove the false claim at docs/coding-standards.md:689, and either wire a real Rule-0 check (a grep over lib/core/database/tables/*.dart primaryKey declarations, or a lint over DAO WHERE clauses) into `make audit`, or downgrade the doc's [E] tag to [P].
acceptance_criteria: A new test (e.g. in goal_dao_test.dart / bookmark_dao_test.dart / stage_dao_test.dart) creates two profiles, inserts a row for profile A, calls the DAO's update/delete method with profile A's row id from a profile-B context, and asserts the row is unchanged / the call is rejected.

goal_repository_impl.updateGoal/deleteGoal (and any other caller found via `grep -rn 'DaoBaseDao\|getGoalById\|getBookmarkById\|getLearningOrderById\|getStageDefinitionById'`) verify existing.profileId against the caller's bound profile before mutating.
docs/coding-standards.md:689 either matches a real `make audit` check or is corrected to state the gap.

findings.title: Wrap point_config_dao.seedDefaults, study_day_config_dao.seedDefaults, and track_learning_order_dao.upsertOrder in a transaction

evidence.quote:
for (final d in fallbackDefaults) {
        await insertConfig(

for (var i = 0; i < refs.length; i++) {
      await into(trackLearningOrder).insert(

findings.why: None of these three multi-row writers is wrapped in `db.transaction()`. If the app is killed/backgrounded mid-loop (routine on mobile), the row set is left partially written. The clearest user-visible case: track_learning_order_dao.upsertOrder is called from saveSedarimOrder/saveMasechtosOrder (lib/features/tracks/track_order/data/repositories/track_learning_order_repository_impl.dart) with the full reordered item list — tens of refs for a masechtos reorder. A crash partway through leaves some refs at their new sortOrder and others at stale values, silently scrambling the track's learning order with no error surfaced. point_config_dao.seedDefaults has a similar exposure (a stage left with no PointConfig row); study_day_config_dao.seedDefaults is lower-risk because isStudyDay() defaults a missing row to 'study' anyway.
findings.recommendation: Wrap each loop body in `await db.transaction(() async { ... })` so the whole seed/reorder either fully applies or fully rolls back.
acceptance_criteria: seedDefaults (both DAOs) and upsertOrder execute inside db.transaction().
A regression test forces a failure on a middle iteration (e.g. a duplicate/invalid row) and asserts none of the batch's rows persisted (all-or-nothing).

findings.title: Replace awaited per-row insert/update loops with Drift batch() in curriculum_scope_dao, stage_dao, and track_dao.purgeHistory

evidence.quote:
for (final value in scopeValues) {
        await into(curriculumScopes).insert(

for (final stage in stages) {
        await insertStageDefinition(stage);

for (final stage in stages) {
        await insertStageDefinition(stage);

findings.why: These four loops are all already inside a db.transaction() (so DB-2 is satisfied — no partial-write risk), but each issues N sequential awaited statements where Drift's batch() would send one. track_dao.purgeHistory is the worst case: on 'delete and wipe history' for a track with hundreds of completions, it round-trips once per row to stamp purgedAt instead of one batched UPDATE. The three sites from the companion DB-2 finding (point_config_dao.seedDefaults, study_day_config_dao.seedDefaults, track_learning_order_dao.upsertOrder) share the identical pattern and compound this once they're wrapped in a transaction.
findings.recommendation: Convert each loop to `batch((b) { for (...) { b.insert(...)/b.update(...); } })`, which Drift supports for both inserts and per-row updates with distinct WHERE clauses inside one batch call.
acceptance_criteria: curriculum_scope_dao.setScopes, stage_dao.replaceStagesForTrack/replaceStagesForCurriculum, and track_dao.purgeHistory's tombstone step use batch() instead of a per-row await loop.
Existing tests for these methods pass unchanged (behavior-preserving refactor).

findings.title: Make SacredWindowDao's cache replace atomic — clearAll()+insertAll() must be one transaction, not the caller's fire-and-forget chain
findings.why: The DAO's own doc comment says '[clearAll] + [insertAll] are called together... Expects the caller to have called [clearAll] first so the table stays coherent' — but the DAO exposes no atomic way to do that, and the only caller (SacredWindowRepository._persistToDb) chains them with `.then(...).ignore()`: unawaited, no transaction, errors silently discarded. If the process dies (routine on mobile backgrounding) between clearAll() completing and insertAll() completing, sacred_window_entries is left empty. That table is the documented source of truth for 'background notification-fire-time checks... without the Flutter engine' (DNI-367) — an empty table means Sacred Time notification suppression silently fails open on next cold-start check, with no error anywhere (`.ignore()` explicitly suppresses it). invalidate() → _persistToDb runs on every location/timezone change and app resume, so the window isn't rare.
findings.recommendation: Add a single `SacredWindowDao.replaceAll(List<SacredWindowEntriesCompanion> entries)` that wraps clearAll+insertAll in one `db.transaction()`, and have sacred_window_repository.dart call that instead of the `.then().ignore()` chain. If fire-and-forget is intentional, at minimum log the failure via AppLogger instead of `.ignore()`.
acceptance_criteria: SacredWindowDao exposes an atomic replaceAll(); sacred_window_repository.dart no longer calls clearAll()/insertAll() separately.
A test makes insertAll throw mid-write inside replaceAll and asserts the table still holds the PREVIOUS rows (no empty-table window), not a partially-cleared state.

findings.title: Split completion_dao.dart, points_balance_dao.dart, track_dao.dart, and completion_dao_extended_test.dart under the 400-line AG-3 cap
findings.why: All four are more than 2x the 400-line hand-written-file cap. completion_dao.dart mixes cross-profile-scope-guarded reads, raw-SQL tier filtering, and grouped aggregates in one file; points_balance_dao.dart mixes balance/ledger/redemption CRUD with sync-outbox plumbing; track_dao.dart mixes lifecycle CRUD with two different multi-table transactional delete flows. Long files raise the odds that the next edit misses a nearby invariant (e.g. the DB-3 loop found in track_dao.dart's purgeHistory, buried 400 lines in).

A Rule-0 line-count check (e.g. `find lib -name '*.dart' ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>400'`) is added to `make audit` and passes.

findings.title: Stop catching StateError (an Error subtype) in user_profile_dao.dart's AccountX.accountTier getter
findings.why: `StateError` extends `Error` in dart:core, and `UserTierX.fromDb` throws it specifically for an unrecognized `tier` string — i.e. local DB corruption or a missed enum-value migration. Catching it here and silently returning `UserTier.localBorn` masks that bug: a `cloudBorn` account whose stored tier string ever drifts (bad migration, hand-edited row, future enum rename) silently behaves as local-born everywhere accountTier is read (sync gating, balance-row eligibility per 'Adults never have balance rows (Rule 3)', etc.), with nothing logged.
findings.recommendation: Let the StateError propagate (or catch and rethrow after an AppLogger.error call) instead of returning a silent fallback — an unrecognized tier value is a bug that should be loud, not a normal control-flow case.
acceptance_criteria: AccountX.accountTier no longer has an `on StateError` handler that returns a default value.
A test asserts that an Account row with an unrecognized `tier` string causes accountTier to throw (or to log via AppLogger and rethrow), not silently return localBorn.

findings.title: Replace track_dao.dart's stringly-typed TrackState class with a real Dart enum
findings.why: TrackState is a 4-value closed lifecycle (active/retired/archived/deleted) central to this HOTSPOT file's whole model, modeled as bare String constants on a TextColumn with no DB-level or compiler-level check that only these 4 values ever get stored. Any code that branches on `.state` gets no exhaustiveness checking, and nothing stops a typo'd string reaching the column (mitigated today only by everyone remembering to use the TrackState.* constants rather than literals — a convention, not a guarantee).
findings.recommendation: Model TrackState as a real Dart `enum` (or use Drift's `.withConverter` to store it as text but expose an enum in Dart), so switches over track state are compiler-exhaustive and no non-member string can be constructed.
acceptance_criteria: TrackState is a Dart enum (or enum-backed column); all TrackState.active-style call sites in this batch keep compiling.
Any switch/when over the state value is exhaustive without a default/_ arm.

findings.title: Add a schema-version floor guard for UserDatabase — onUpgrade has no path below v25

evidence.quote:
onUpgrade: (Migrator m, int from, int to) async {
        if (from < 25) {

findings.why: git log -p on user_database.dart shows onUpgrade previously handled `if (from < 3)` through `if (from < 23)`; commit 9612d7a0 deleted that whole range and its own diff changes the docstring from '...schemaVersion bumped to 12; all old migration steps deleted' to describing a second 'W3.19 rebuild' wipe-install boundary. Today onUpgrade only starts at `from < 25`. database_provider.dart opens UserDatabase directly via driftDatabase(name: dbName) with no version-floor check at all — unlike ContentDatabase, which SeedManager guards with an explicit version comparison plus atomic replace before Drift ever touches it. Any real device whose local user_database.db is still at a schemaVersion below 25 will, on next launch, run onUpgrade(from=<old>, to=32): none of the intervening table-rename/profileId/FK changes apply, but Drift still stamps PRAGMA user_version=32 afterward — the on-disk schema stays frozen at its old shape while every DAO assumes v32's shape, so the first query throws 'no such column'/'no such table', or silently misreads a same-named-but-differently-typed column. coding-standards.md states as a current fact (2026-07-02) that 'the user DB is at schemaVersion 32 with real on-device data and no server backup', which is exactly the population this gap would hit. What would confirm real-world exposure: crash telemetry for 'no such column'/'no such table' immediately post-update, or checking whether any distributed build ever shipped schemaVersion 2-24 to non-dev devices before the WS7/v25 bump.
findings.recommendation: Add a pre-open guard (mirroring SeedManager's pattern) that reads PRAGMA user_version via raw sqlite3 before handing the file to Drift; if it's below the lowest version this onUpgrade body actually handles, run a documented recovery path (backup + fresh onCreate) instead of letting Drift silently half-upgrade. Longer term, adopt DB-4's drift_schemas/ + migrateAndValidate tests so a future 'delete old migration steps' edit fails CI instead of shipping silently.
acceptance_criteria: A regression test opens a DB stamped with a low PRAGMA user_version (e.g. 2) and asserts the app either migrates it correctly through to 32 or safely detects-and-recovers — it must never end up with user_version=32 stamped over pre-v25 table shape.
database_provider.dart (or a new guard module) checks on-disk PRAGMA user_version against a documented MIN_SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION before opening via Drift.
DB-4's drift_schemas/ export + generated migration tests land so a future deletion of an `if (from < N)` block fails CI.

findings.title: Wrap DeviceRegistryDatabase.removeAccount's delete + state-clear in a transaction()

evidence.quote:
for (var i = 1; i < group.length; i++) {
        removed += await removeAccount(group[i].accountId);

findings.why: removeAccount's own docstring says it clears lastActiveAccountId 'so the next launch does NOT silently auto-activate an arbitrary fallback account against a dangling pointer (D10)' — but the delete and the pointer-clear are two separately-awaited statements with no db.transaction() around them. If the process dies between them (routine on Android when a backgrounded app is reclaimed, and account removal is exactly the kind of action a user triggers then backgrounds), the delete commits but the clear never runs, leaving deviceState.lastActiveAccountId pointing at a row that no longer exists — the exact D10 state device_registry_test.dart's 'removeAccount clears it when removing the ACTIVE account (D10)' test checks for, just reached through a crash path the in-memory test can't simulate. dedupeByEmail compounds this by calling removeAccount N times in an unwrapped loop, so a mid-run crash also leaves a partially-merged duplicate-account state. Every other multi-write DAO in this codebase (stage_dao.dart, curriculum_scope_dao.dart, user_profile_dao.dart, track_dao.dart, points_balance_dao.dart) wraps its writes in transaction() — this file is the outlier.

findings.title: Fix ContentTree.parent()'s off-by-one when a leaf precedes its container in source order
findings.rule: Correctness bug (Fowler duplicated-but-inconsistent logic between pass 1 and pass 2)
findings.why: Empirically verified: constructed a 4-level Bavli fixture where the leaf item ('Berakhot 2a:1') appears before its own container ('Berakhot 2a') in the input list, called ContentTree.fromCurricula(...).parent('Berakhot 2a:1'), and got 'Berakhot 2' (the grandparent/daf-level container) instead of the correct immediate parent 'Berakhot 2a'. Root cause: for a leaf, `_ancestorLevels(item)` already returns the PARENT container's own key (that's its documented purpose, and pass 1 at lines 110-121 uses it directly with no further truncation). Pass 2 treats `levels` uniformly as if it were the item's own key and applies a second `.sublist(0, length - 1)` 'walk up one level' step — which, for leaves, walks up an extra level past the true parent. Pass 1 resolves leaves correctly when their container is registered first; pass 2's fallback only fires — with the wrong answer — when a leaf is encountered before its container. ContentTree.parent() currently has zero callers in lib/ (content_hierarchy_screen.dart uses only .children()/.containerFor()), so this is not live-user-visible today, but it is a public, documented, keepAlive-cached API on the exact class whose stated purpose is 'O(1) parent/child/adjacent traversal' — the first feature that calls .parent() for breadcrumb 'up' navigation inherits a silently-wrong result whenever source ordering isn't strictly parent-before-child.
findings.recommendation: In pass 2's leaf branch, use `ancestorLevels` (the value already returned by _ancestorLevels) directly as the parent container key, the same way pass 1 does — do not apply an additional sublist(0, length-1) truncation for leaves.
acceptance_criteria: A regression test at test/core/content/content_tree_test.dart builds a curriculum with a leaf listed before its own container and asserts ContentTree.parent(leafRef) returns the immediate parent, not the grandparent.

findings.title: Log Firebase/App Check init failures in firebase_bootstrap.dart instead of swallowing them silently

evidence.quote:
} catch (_) {
  // App Check unavailable — continue; sync may be rejected if enforced.

} catch (_) {
  // Firebase init failed — app continues in local-first mode.

findings.why: Both catches are comment-only (no AppLogger call), so they pass the built-in empty_catches lint (which accepts a comment as content) but violate EH-3's log-less clause. AppLogger.instance is lazily constructable at this point (bootstrap.dart calls bootstrapFirebase() before AppLogger.init(), but AppLogger.instance auto-initializes on first access), so logging was possible and simply omitted. If Firebase.initializeApp() or App Check activation fails in production (corrupt Installation ID, blocked network, Play Services missing), the app correctly falls back to local-first mode but leaves zero diagnostic trail anywhere — not even a local Talker entry — making 'sync never works on this install' field reports undiagnosable.
findings.recommendation: Add an AppLogger.instance.warning/error call with a stable event code in each catch before falling through, e.g. `AppLogger.instance.error(event: 'firebase_init_failed', exception: e, stackTrace: s)`.
acceptance_criteria: Both catch blocks in firebase_bootstrap.dart call AppLogger.instance.{warning,error} with a stable event code before continuing.
A test that injects a throwing Firebase.initializeApp (or App Check activate) stub and asserts an error/warning log event fires.
A Rule-0 grep/lint flags any catch block in lib/ that neither rethrows/converts nor calls AppLogger (EH-3 currently has no checker).

findings.title: Stop showing raw e.toString() as the device-restore error message in RestoreStatus/DeviceRestoreService
findings.rule: EH-5 / AX-2 (no pre-formatted human messages; ARB-only user text)
findings.why: RestoreStatus.error(message: String) is a raw String, not a code/enum, and DeviceRestoreService feeds it e.toString() directly — a raw exception message (e.g. 'Exception: Data pull failed: [firebase_firestore/unavailable] ...'). device_restore_screen.dart renders this string verbatim next to a properly-localized l10n.deviceRestoreFailed headline (lines 214-222), so any restore failure — plausible on flaky mobile networks, which this cloud-restore flow specifically targets — shows raw, untranslated, technical English text to Hebrew-locale users today, live, with no masking guard. Separately, RestoreStatus.restoring's `phase` field is a hardcoded English sentence matched by string equality in _localizePhase(); the two files' string literals must stay in lockstep by convention only — if either drifts, the fallback silently renders the raw English phase instead of erroring.
findings.recommendation: Replace RestoreStatus.error's free-text `message` with a stable error code/enum resolved via AppLocalizations in the screen (mirroring how `phase` already works, but with a sealed type instead of string matching so drift is a compile error).
acceptance_criteria: RestoreStatus.error carries a typed code (enum or sealed subtype), not a raw String built from e.toString().
A Locale('he') widget test pumps a forced restore failure and asserts the rendered error text is 100% ARB-sourced (no raw exception text).
phase and the error code share one sealed type/enum between DeviceRestoreService and the screen so an unmapped case fails to compile instead of silently falling back to English.

findings.title: Remove duplicate top-level keys in app_en.arb — they silently shadow earlier definitions and the parity checker can't see it
findings.rule: AX-2 (ARB integrity) / Rule 0 gap in tool/arb_parity_check.dart

evidence.quote: "notificationReminderBody": "{taskCount,plural, =0{No tasks today — stay on track!} =1{...} other{...}}",
"notificationReminderBody": "You have {taskCount, plural, =1{1 task} other{{taskCount} tasks}} across ... today",
final enMap = jsonDecode(enFile.readAsStringSync()) as Map<String, dynamic>;

findings.why: app_en.arb defines 5 keys twice each (todaysLearning, errorLoadingTasks, today, notificationReminderTitle, notificationReminderBody — verified via a full-file duplicate-key scan, not sampling). JSON silently keeps only the last occurrence, and I confirmed via the generated app_localizations_en.dart that the LAST definition always wins: today ships as 'Today' (line 2200) not 'TODAY' (line 433, dead); notificationReminderBody ships WITHOUT the friendlier zero-task branch authored at line 1938 ('No tasks today — stay on track!') — the later, lesser definition at line 2834 (no =0 case) is what's actually generated. That specific gap is currently masked because notification_providers.dart's D2 fix cancels the reminder instead of calling this method when taskCount==0 — but the dead ARB content and the blind spot are real: tool/arb_parity_check.dart uses jsonDecode, which structurally cannot see intra-file duplicate keys (it only diffs the already-deduped EN/HE key SETS), so this class of bug has no tooling coverage at all and could recur invisibly.
findings.recommendation: Delete the stale first definitions (lines 15, 397, 433, 1937-1938) keeping one definition per key, and extend the parity checker to detect duplicate raw top-level keys.
acceptance_criteria: app_en.arb has exactly one definition per top-level key (verified by a duplicate-key scan over the raw text, not just jsonDecode).

findings.title: Fix app_shell.dart's fixed-height context banners — they truncate text under accessibility scaling and undersize the exit-button tap targets
findings.rule: AX-4 (no fixed heights on text wrappers; 48dp targets)
findings.why: _ChildViewBanner (height: 28), TutorModeIndicatorBar (height: 24), and ProfileSwitcherBar (height: 44) are hardcoded-height Containers wrapping Text with maxLines:1/overflow:ellipsis and fontSize 11-14; none of them scale with MediaQuery.textScaler. At a larger accessibility text-scale setting, a real, present-day user segment sees the child/talmid name or role badge clipped tighter than intended, or the row overflowing the fixed bar. Independent of text scale, the Exit buttons in the first two banners are geometrically provable to be under the 48dp minimum: an icon(12)+padding(vertical:2x2)+text(11sp) inside a 24-28dp-tall parent caps the whole tap target at roughly 20-24dp — well short of 48dp — for a control (exiting parent/tutor mode) that a stressed or motor-impaired user needs to hit reliably.
findings.recommendation: Let the banner Containers size to content (IntrinsicHeight or padding-driven, not a literal height:), and grow the Exit InkWell's hit area to kMinInteractiveDimension via padding/ConstrainedBox independent of the visual bar height.
acceptance_criteria: _ChildViewBanner, TutorModeIndicatorBar, and ProfileSwitcherBar no longer hardcode a literal `height:` that can clip scaled text.
A widget test pumped at TextScaler.linear(1.3)+ and Locale('he') asserts no RenderFlex overflow and no truncated semantics label on these three banners.

findings.title: Close the DeviceRegistryDatabase connection on account_bootstrap.dart's exception path
findings.why: `registry.close()` sits at the end of the try block, not in a finally. If sessionService.resolveActiveAccountId() (line 30) or registry.findById() (line 33) throws, execution jumps straight to the outer catch (line 51), which logs and returns a fallback filename WITHOUT ever closing the Drift-backed device_registry connection — the exact 'I/O fails halfway' scenario the Nygard lens asks about. Impact is low in practice (this runs once per app process at startup), but a leaked native database handle held for the app's whole lifetime is still an avoidable defect, and it would compound if this code path were ever retried (e.g. a future hot-reattempt) or re-used in a longer-lived context.
findings.recommendation: Move `final registry = ...` construction above a try/finally (or wrap the resolveActiveAccountId/findById calls in try{...}finally{ await registry.close(); }) so every exit path closes the connection.
acceptance_criteria: registry.close() executes on both the success path and any exception path out of bootstrapAccount.

findings.title: Fix CurriculumLabel.item breadcrumb/parent modes to resolve ancestor Hebrew names, not just the leaf's

findings.title: Add profileId FK+CASCADE to 6 tables — tutored-mirror wipe currently orphans a mirrored child's data
findings.rule: profileId-in-PK Invariant / DB-6 (sync-able entity integrity, FK-cascade discipline)

evidence.quote: the learner_profiles row cascades to all mirrored rows in completions, ... curriculum_tracks, etc. No explicit child-row deletion is needed.
The FK `ON DELETE CASCADE` on every child table (completions, streak_events, learning_ledger, bookmarks, goals, etc.)
// `outbox` has no FK — without this its pending pushes for the deleted profile would survive.

findings.why: None of these 6 tables declare `.references(LearnerProfiles, #id, onDelete: KeyAction.cascade)` on their profileId column (every sibling table that IS correctly protected does). `ProfileRepositoryImpl.deleteProfile()` compensates by explicitly deleting from all 6 before removing the profile row — the team clearly knows about this gap. But `TutoredMirrorWipeService.wipeMirrorForGrant/wipeAllMirrors/wipeRevokedMirrors` (used on tutor grant revoke/resign, tutor sign-out, and the D18 revoke-reconcile path) does NOT replicate that compensation — it only calls `ProfileDao.deleteTutoredMirrorByGrantId`, a bare delete of the `learner_profiles` row, while its own top-of-file comment incorrectly asserts universal FK cascade covering `curriculum_tracks, etc.`. `tutored_pull_service.dart` (line 99, 'a point_configs FK violation') confirms these tables are actually populated for a live mirror. Net effect: when a tutoring relationship ends, the tutored child's mirrored curriculum_tracks/daily_plans/point_configs/profile_programs/study_day_configs rows silently persist on the tutor's device forever — a child-privacy data-retention failure that contradicts the code's own stated invariant, with no error or log to reveal it.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) add `.references(LearnerProfiles, #id, onDelete: KeyAction.cascade)` to profileId on all 6 tables (schema migration + schema export per DB-4), or (b) make `TutoredMirrorWipeService` explicitly delete from all 6 tables before removing the `learner_profiles` row, mirroring `ProfileRepositoryImpl.deleteProfile`'s existing pattern (no migration needed, lower risk, matches established precedent). Fix the false comment either way.
acceptance_criteria: New regression test: after wipeMirrorForGrant/wipeAllMirrors, querying curriculum_tracks/daily_plans/outbox/point_configs/profile_programs/study_day_configs WHERE profileId = <wiped id> returns 0 rows.
tutored_mirror_wipe_service.dart's header comment no longer claims universal FK cascade for tables that don't have it.

tool/schema_check.dart (or a new companion checker) flags any core/database/tables profileId column lacking a `.references(LearnerProfiles, ...)` FK, so a future new table can't silently reintroduce the gap.

findings.title: Add UNIQUE(profileId, ulid) to PointsLedger and RewardRedemptions — sync merge can double-credit a child's points
findings.rule: DB-6 (sync-able entity integrity) / profileId-in-PK's composite-index companion requirement
findings.why: PointsLedger and RewardRedemptions both carry a `ulid` column documented as "cross-device id for append-only cloud sync" — the exact same purpose LearningLedger's `ulid` serves, where it is protected by a real `UNIQUE(profileId, ulid)` @TableIndex. Neither PointsLedger nor RewardRedemptions has any uniqueKeys/@TableIndex at all. PointsLedgerMerger's own comment says entries are "deduplicated on ulid via INSERT-OR-IGNORE," but points_balance_dao.dart's insertRemoteLedgerEntryIfAbsent actually does a manual SELECT-then-INSERT with no DB constraint backing it — a classic TOCTOU race. If two merge calls for the same ulid ever interleave (concurrent pulls, a retried tutored pull, a future refactor that parallelizes merges), a duplicate row lands; reDeriveBalanceFromLedger sums ALL ledger deltas, so the child's points balance silently becomes wrong — violating the table's own documented invariant that balance is "the authoritative denormalised sum of all ledger entries."
findings.recommendation: Add `@TableIndex(name: 'points_ledger_profile_ulid', columns: {#profileId, #ulid}, unique: true)` to PointsLedger and an equivalent unique index to RewardRedemptions (mirroring learning_ledger.dart), ship as a schema migration, and switch insertRemoteLedgerEntryIfAbsent to rely on that constraint (insertOnConflictDoNothing) instead of a separate SELECT.
acceptance_criteria: Schema migration adds the unique index to points_ledger and reward_redemptions, with committed schema export + generated migration test (DB-4).
Regression test: calling the merge path twice concurrently (Future.wait) with the same ulid results in exactly one row and exactly one balance credit.

findings.title: Redact TransactionalEmail.plaintextBody before logging in LoggingTransactionalEmailService.send()
findings.rule: Child-privacy logging hygiene (PV-family principle) — breaks the PiiRedactor.sensitiveKeys contract in core/logging/logger.dart that the same function's sibling field already relies on

evidence.quote: '$tutorEmail has declined your invitation to tutor $childName.\n\n'

findings.why: LoggingTransactionalEmailService.send() (the only bound TransactionalEmailService implementation today) logs the full plaintextBody under the key 'body' via AppLogger.instance.debug(). PiiRedactor.redactFields() only blanks values whose KEY is in the 49-entry sensitiveKeys allowlist (logger.dart:203-251) — 'body' is not in it, even though 'to'/'recipient'/'email_to' were deliberately added and regression-tested (test/core/logging/logger_extended_test.dart:271-304, tag V2-R5 C2) for the exact same call site two lines above. TutorDeclinedEmail, TutorResignedEmail and TutorGrantRevokedEmail are already constructed and sent today from tutor_notification_service.dart (decline/resign/revoke flows), so a child's name and a tutor's raw email address (embedded in TutorDeclinedEmail's prose body) land in the log buffer in cleartext on every one of those events. That buffer is exactly what features/settings/.../send_logs_service.dart uploads (unfiltered by level, last 10 minutes) to `users/{uid}/diagnostic_logs/` in Firestore, a collection its own docstring says a developer can view/query directly in the Firebase console. Once TutorInviteEmail (defined but not yet wired) goes live, the same gap will additionally leak the invite deep link. This directly contradicts the redaction guarantee the codebase already built and tested for the sibling 'to' field in the same function.
findings.recommendation: Add 'body' (or a dedicated key such as 'email_body') to PiiRedactor.sensitiveKeys in core/logging/logger.dart, or stop passing plaintextBody to the logger entirely (log email.runtimeType/a template id instead of the rendered body). Extend the existing V2-R5 C2 test group in test/core/logging/logger_extended_test.dart to cover the debug() 'Payload' call the same way it already covers the warning() call.
acceptance_criteria: PiiRedactor.redactFields({'body': 'contains tutor@example.com and a child name'})['body'] == '[REDACTED]', or LoggingTransactionalEmailService.send() no longer logs the raw plaintextBody at all

Worse, dio_client_test.dart (158 lines) and fetcher_test.dart (831 lines) — 989 of my batch's 1188 lines — thoroughly test createDioClient/createSefariaClient/RetryInterceptor and the 7 fetchers, none of which the live pipeline calls: seed_content.dart builds its own untested, retry-less, logger-less Dio() inline (line 26) instead of reusing the fully-tested createSefariaClient(). This is a large, continuously-CI-run, thoroughly-documented dead branch that will mislead a future contributor fixing a Sefaria-shape regression into 'fixing' code nothing runs, while docs/explainers/content-database.md and docs/source-tree-analysis.md still list seed_content.dart as if it's live, contradicting docs/seed-build.md.

acceptance_criteria: grep -rn 'CurriculumContentFetcher\|createSefariaClient\|createDioClient' across lib/ and tool/ shows either zero results (deleted) or a real caller in tool/seed_content.dart (reconnected)

findings.title: Convert ContentItem/CurriculumHierarchyConfig/FetchResult to @freezed instead of hand-rolled or absent equality
findings.rule: Naming/placement/invariants — 'Domain/state models are immutable @freezed classes ... never hand-write ==/hashCode for data classes — hand-rolled equality drifts from the fields and silently breaks rebuild-skipping.'
findings.why: ContentItem's == compares only curriculumId+sefariaRef, silently ignoring level1-4/displayNameHe/displayNameEn/sortOrder/isLeaf — two items differing only in display text or sort order compare equal, so any future Set/Map-keyed-by-item or equality-based diff would silently drop a real change. CurriculumHierarchyConfig has no == at all (falls back to identity), so two field-identical instances are never equal, AND exposes a directly-mutable List<String> levelLabels with no defensive copy — content_repository_impl.dart caches these instances in _configCache and hands the same object to every reader, so one caller mutating the list would corrupt it for all subsequent readers. FetchResult (the public return type of fetchAllContent()) has the same gap.
findings.recommendation: Make all three @freezed with generated ==/hashCode/copyWith; for CurriculumHierarchyConfig use an immutable list wrapper (e.g. List.unmodifiable or IList) for levelLabels.
acceptance_criteria: dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs regenerates these as @freezed with no manual ==/hashCode remaining
a regression test proves two ContentItems differing only in sortOrder/displayNameHe are NOT ==
levelLabels cannot be mutated through the public CurriculumHierarchyConfig API

findings.title: Rewrite ConnectivityGateway's only test — it is tautologically true and hits the real network
findings.rule: TQ-6 (hermetic tests: no network) + TQ-8 (assertion weaker than what the source can do wrong)
findings.why: isOffline is defined as the literal negation of isOnline, so expect(online, isNot(offline)) reduces to 'online == online' — true for every possible return value, including if isOnline were hardcoded to `return true;`. The test can never catch a regression in the actual DNS-lookup logic. Because ConnectivityGateway has no injectable seam for the lookup, the test cannot fake a response either way and instead performs a live DNS query to dns.google on every run — flaky/slow/blocked in network-restricted CI or sandboxes, and this is the class's only test.
findings.recommendation: Add an injectable lookup function (e.g. `Future<List<InternetAddress>> Function(String)`, defaulting to InternetAddress.lookup) to ConnectivityGateway, then test both the true and false paths via a fake with zero real network access.
acceptance_criteria: test asserts isOnline == true for a faked successful lookup and == false for a faked SocketException/timeout
test suite passes with network access disabled

findings.title: Make the 'All fetchers cover all 7 curricula' test verify against CurriculumId.values instead of a hand-maintained map
findings.rule: TQ-8 (assertion weaker than what the source can actually do wrong)

evidence.quote:
// All 7 curricula with dedicated fetchers.
      expect(fetchers.length, 7);

findings.why: The test's title claims 'each CurriculumId has a corresponding fetcher' but it only checks internal self-consistency of a hardcoded 7-entry map — it never iterates CurriculumId.values. CurriculumId actually has 9 values; only 'tanach' is registered in CompositeCurriculumStrategy._registry as fetcher-exempt (composite of chumash+nach). 'mishnehTorah' is neither composite nor present in the fetcher map nor backed by any class in tool/lib/sefaria/, yet the test passes regardless — a curriculum can silently lack fetcher coverage forever without this 'coverage' test ever turning red. (Whether mishneh_torah.json is actually correct today is not established here — the defect is that this test cannot detect the gap either way.)
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the test to iterate CurriculumId.values, skip ids where CompositeCurriculumStrategy.isComposite(id.storageKey) is true, and assert every remaining id has a fetcher entry.
acceptance_criteria: Test fails today (before any fetcher is added) if run against the corrected assertion, proving it actually detects the mishnehTorah gap
Test passes once mishnehTorah is either registered composite or given a real fetcher

findings.title: Cancel or document the leaked DNS-lookup Future in ConnectivityGateway.isOnline on timeout
findings.rule: Nygard lens — what happens when I/O fails halfway
findings.why: Future.timeout() races a Timer against the lookup but cannot cancel the underlying OS-level DNS resolution — dart:io gives no cancellable primitive for InternetAddress.lookup. Under packet loss or a captive portal (exactly when this check matters most), the original lookup keeps running past the 2s timeout with no way to observe or cancel it; repeated calls (e.g. retrying a failed offline-account conversion in account_actions.dart) can accumulate abandoned lookups.
findings.recommendation: Either document the accepted tradeoff inline (dart:io has no cancellable DNS API) with a bounded-impact justification, or switch to a primitive that supports cancellation (e.g. a raw socket connect with explicit close on timeout).
acceptance_criteria: Either an inline comment documents the accepted leak and its bound, or a test demonstrates no more than one lookup stays in flight after repeated rapid isOnline calls under a simulated timeout

findings.title: Use `is TalkerDioLogger` instead of a runtimeType.toString() string match in dio_client_test.dart

findings.recommendation: Import package:talker_dio_logger/talker_dio_logger.dart and replace the check with `dio.interceptors.any((i) => i is TalkerDioLogger)`.
acceptance_criteria: Test uses an `is` type check, no runtimeType.toString() comparison remains, test still passes

findings.title: Delete dead core/navigation re-export shims and break the app_router↔guards import cycle
findings.rule: coding-standards.md:63 "dependency direction is strictly app → features → core"; adjacent to Rule 2's "do not add other barrel/re-export files"

findings.title: Rename core/utils/date_utils.dart's DateUtils class off the Flutter SDK's own DateUtils name
findings.rule: AG-4 (public top-level symbol names unique across lib/)
findings.why: package:flutter/material.dart exports its own `abstract final class DateUtils` (src/material/date.dart:247, re-exported at material.dart:65) with methods like isSameDay/getDaysInMonth used elsewhere in this repo (e.g. monthly_activity_sliver_calendar.dart calls Flutter's DateUtils.getDaysInMonth). This project's core/utils/date_utils.dart declares a second, unrelated `class DateUtils` with different semantics (isSameLocalDay is deliberately UTC→local-day aware per the P5 streak-boundary pattern; Flutter's isSameDay is a raw field compare). At least 14 lib/ files and 25+ test files import both material.dart and this file unqualified; exactly one file (goal_setup_screen.dart:1) already needed `hide DateUtils` to compile because it calls the project's DateUtils.extractLocalDate. Any of the other ~39 files is one `DateUtils.` autocomplete away from either a hard "ambiguous import" compile error or — if an agent "fixes" it by hiding the wrong side — silently swapping in Flutter's timezone-naive comparison where the streak-safe local-day comparison was intended, a domain the whole file exists to get right.
findings.recommendation: Rename the project's class (e.g. LocalDayUtils) or fold its 4 static methods into DateTimeFactory in the same file, so it no longer shadows the Flutter SDK name. Remove goal_setup_screen.dart's now-unnecessary `hide DateUtils` after the rename.
acceptance_criteria: `grep -rn "^class DateUtils" learning_tracker/lib/` returns no matches (class renamed).

findings.title: Remove dead isShabbos/isYomTov/formatHebrewDate from HebrewCalendarUtils (superseded by zmanim_window_service)
findings.rule: Evans lens (ubiquitous language re-derived, not enforced in one place) + dead code

evidence.quote: /// For precise zmanim (sunset/nightfall), use ComplexZmanimCalendar with a GeoLocation.

findings.why: `grep -rn` across all of lib/ finds zero production callers of isShabbos, isYomTov, or formatHebrewDate outside their own definition file — only test/core/utils/hebrew_calendar_utils_test.dart and one story-acceptance test call isShabbos, testing code nothing else ever runs. Meanwhile lib/features/sacred_time/domain/services/zmanim_window_service.dart implements the real, GeoLocation/zmanim-aware Shabbos+Yom-Tov window (candle-lighting offset, tzais, JewishCalendar.isAssurBemelacha) that actually drives the Sacred Time lock feature — and isShabbos's own doc comment admits its 18:00-local-clock-hour heuristic is inferior ("For precise zmanim... use ComplexZmanimCalendar with a GeoLocation"). Because this dead code lives in core/utils/ (importable by any feature — Rule 1 only blocks core→features, not the reverse) and is unit-tested (making it look supported), a future feature needing "is it Shabbos right now" is one natural-language search away from wiring up the crude, timezone-naive version instead of the correct geo-aware one — and if the caller passes a UTC DateTime (the P5-mandated storage format everywhere else in this codebase), isShabbos's `.hour >= 18` check reads UTC hour, not true local hour, silently wrong for any locale far from UTC.
findings.recommendation: Delete isShabbos, isYomTov, and formatHebrewDate (and their test coverage) from HebrewCalendarUtils. If a lightweight non-geo fallback is genuinely wanted somewhere, rename it to make the approximation explicit (e.g. isApproximateShabbosNoGeo) and doc-link to zmanim_window_service.dart as the source of truth.
acceptance_criteria: `grep -rn "isShabbos\|isYomTov\|formatHebrewDate" learning_tracker/lib/` shows zero references outside sacred_time/ (or the methods are removed entirely).

findings.title: Replace date_utils_test.dart's real DateTime.now() read with a fixed/injected clock
findings.why: This is the only wall-clock read across all 14 test files in the batch — every other test in the suite (and in the file's own source, date_utils.dart, which is explicitly designed around a swappable LocalDayClock so "day-boundary semantics are deterministic in tests") uses fixed DateTime.utc(...) literals. Comparing DateTimeFactory.nowUtc() against a freshly-read DateTime.now() with a 1-second tolerance is a live flake source: any CI scheduling jitter, GC pause, or slow VM startup between the two calls pushes the gap over 1 second and fails the test for a reason unrelated to the code under test.
findings.recommendation: Override the LocalDayClock with a fixed fake instant (per the source file's own documented pattern: `localDayClockProvider.overrideWithValue(...)` or `useLocalDayClock`) and assert DateTimeFactory.nowUtc() returns exactly that fixed instant, rather than "close to real time".
acceptance_criteria: No `DateTime.now()` call remains in test/core/utils/date_utils_test.dart.

findings.title: Inject ParentAnalyticsRepository into RestoreGuard instead of constructing it inline
findings.rule: SM-7 (repositories/services/DAOs constructed only inside their @riverpod provider or a test override)
findings.why: RestoreGuard._resolve() hand-constructs ParentAnalyticsRepositoryImpl(db) directly inside the navigation-check method rather than receiving it as an injected dependency — a literal SM-7 violation. ParentAnalyticsRepository has no Riverpod provider anywhere in the codebase (it's hand-constructed at 2 more sites outside this batch: local_data_upload_service.dart and device_restore_service.dart), so today nothing lets a test or a future caller swap this repository via ProviderScope; a test that wants to fake it has to fake the whole UserDatabase instead. Real-world cost is low today (the class is a thin, stateless DAO wrapper, and RestoreGuard's closure-based constructor is otherwise a deliberately Riverpod-free, easily-testable design — see its excellent test suite), but if SM-7 ships a checker this line (and its 2 siblings) will need either a wrapping provider or a documented exception.
findings.recommendation: Either add a parentAnalyticsRepositoryProvider (@riverpod, takes UserDatabase) and inject it into RestoreGuard's constructor alongside getDatabase, or explicitly document ParentAnalyticsRepositoryImpl as an intentional non-Riverpod infra helper exempt from SM-7.
acceptance_criteria: Once SM-7 has a checker, ParentAnalyticsRepositoryImpl( outside core/analytics/ appears only inside a @riverpod provider body, or is allowlisted with a stated reason.

findings.title: Assert the actual zero value, not just non-emptiness, in streak_state_provider_test.dart's 'stream emits new value' test

evidence.quote:
await Future<void>.delayed(Duration.zero);
      expect(states, isNotEmpty); // zero at start

findings.why: The comment states the intent ('zero at start') but `expect(states, isNotEmpty)` only proves an emission arrived, not that its value is 0 -- a regression that made the initial computed streak nonzero (e.g. a restore/reduce ordering bug) would still pass this line. In practice the invariant IS protected elsewhere in the same file ('emits streak state as a stream' and 'emits empty state when no events', lines 131-141, both assert currentStreak==0 on first emission), so this specific line just doesn't pull its own weight and its comment overclaims what it checks.
findings.recommendation: Change to `expect(states.first, 0); // zero at start`.
acceptance_criteria: Assertion at streak_state_provider_test.dart:166 checks the emitted value equals 0, matching its own comment.

findings.title: Pin StreakStateProvider's day-bucketing seam instead of letting streak_state_provider_test.dart depend on the host machine's timezone
findings.why: read()/watch() call StreakReducer.reduce() without pinning the injectable `dayOf` seam that streak_reducer.dart's own doc comment says exists precisely 'so tests can pin a fixed UTC offset deterministically without depending on the host machine's timezone.' Both FakeLocalDayClock.today() and the default dayOf (DateUtils.extractLocalDate, date_utils.dart:64) resolve through DateTime.toLocal(), which reads the executing machine's TZ -- confirmed empirically inside the real flutter_tester harness: `TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati flutter test` shows DateTime.utc(2026,5,14,12).toLocal() shift a full calendar day. I could not flip any assertion in this specific file under that TZ (ran the suite 3x under the sandbox default Europe/London and once under forced Pacific/Kiritimati, all 13 tests green each time) because every fixture here sits at hour 0 or hour 12 UTC and every current day-gap still lands inside the reducer's +/-1-day grace window either way -- that is a property of today's specific fixture values, not a guarantee. The sibling unit suite (test/features/sync/domain/reducers/streak_reducer_test.dart:120-158) already tests the local-vs-UTC distinction correctly by injecting dayOf directly; this integration-level file has no such seam and inherits toLocal()'s host dependency instead. A fixture pair whose UTC-hour asymmetry straddles a day boundary differently under some real TZ (e.g. clock seeded at 23:00 UTC, event at 01:00 UTC) would confirm an actual flip -- the D17 rollover test already seeds close to a boundary and is the most likely one to trip this by accident in a future edit.
findings.recommendation: Either give StreakStateProvider.read/watch an explicit dayOf override (mirroring the reducer's own seam) or have the test suite pin TZ=UTC explicitly (Makefile/CI env var) so pass/fail can't depend on the runner's locale.
acceptance_criteria: `TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati flutter test test/core/streak/streak_state_provider_test.dart` and the default-TZ run both stay green by construction (pinned dayOf or pinned TZ), not by coincidence of current fixture values.

findings.title: Replace fixed-duration Future.delayed waits with deterministic stream-emission awaits in streak_state_provider_test.dart
findings.why: All four waits (lines 165, 169, 222, 228) assume the DB-watch -> reduce -> controller.add -> listener chain settles within an arbitrary real-time slice, instead of awaiting the stream's actual next emission. Locally this is stable -- ran the file 3x back-to-back plus once under a forced non-UTC TZ, all green every time -- but a busier CI runner, or a slower query added later in StreakRestorer/the watch() chain, can starve the timer past 10ms and produce a flaky red unrelated to the streak logic under test. This exact Future.delayed-as-flush idiom recurs roughly 85 times across ~20 other test files in this repo, so it's a systemic pattern rather than something unique to this file.
findings.recommendation: Await the stream directly (e.g. `await expectLater(states_stream, emitsThrough(predicate))`) or expose an explicit completion signal from the fake instead of guessing a wall-clock delay.
acceptance_criteria: No Future.delayed remains as the sole synchronization mechanism between an async write and a stream-based assertion in this file; assertions instead await the stream's own emission.

findings.title: Add the IL-1 sentinel-0 guard to UseHebrewDate/ShowNikudPref/CurrentTransliterationVariant/CurrentFontSize in preference_providers.dart
findings.rule: SM-2/SM-3 (notifier state consistency across rebuilds) — documented bug class (IL-1) only partially fixed

evidence.quote:
if (profileId == 0 && _hasBindingForRealProfile) {
      // Transient sentinel — keep the last valid state.

final profileId = ref.watch(activeProfileIdProvider);
    final pref = ref.watch(hebrewDatePreferenceProvider);

final profileId = ref.watch(activeProfileIdProvider);
    final pref = ref.watch(nikudPreferenceProvider);

final profileId = ref.watch(activeProfileIdProvider);
    final pref = ref.watch(textDisplayPreferenceProvider);

findings.why: The file's own comment documents that activeProfileIdProvider transiently emits sentinel 0 during the offline-signup DB switch (ref.invalidate(userDatabaseProvider)) before settling back to the real profile id. UseHebrewTerms guards against this; UseHebrewDate, ShowNikudPref, CurrentTransliterationVariant and CurrentFontSize use the byte-for-byte identical ref.watch(activeProfileIdProvider) + _bindObserver(...) shape but have no guard, so each transiently rebinds to profile-0's stored/legacy/default value — visibly flipping the Hebrew-calendar, nikud, transliteration-dialect and font-size settings away from the user's real choice until the id resettles, and silently misfiling any toggle tapped inside that window under profile 0's SharedPreferences key instead of the real profile's.
findings.recommendation: Extract _hasBindingForRealProfile plus the early-return into a small shared helper (e.g. a mixin or a wrapper around _bindObserver) so all 5 sentinel-sensitive notifiers share one implementation instead of one having the fix and four re-deriving (and missing) it.
acceptance_criteria: UseHebrewDate, ShowNikudPref, CurrentTransliterationVariant and CurrentFontSize all preserve state instead of rebinding when profileId==0 after a real profile id was already observed.
Behavioral regression tests (ProviderContainer-based, see companion test-coverage finding) exist for all 5 notifiers driving a real-id -> 0 -> real-id transition.
